learning-loop.title: Learning loop
learning-loop.body: The more you chat, the more your work patterns are captured here. See what RICE has learned and which skills were auto-generated at a glance.

chat-input.title: Chat input
chat-input.body: Send messages to the agent here. Type / to pull up your saved skills instantly — attachments are supported too.

model-settings.title: Model settings
model-settings.body: Check and switch your connected AI model — hosted in the cloud or running locally via Ollama.

my-skills.title: My Skills
my-skills.body: Manage skills auto-generated from chats or built by hand. Run them instantly with / commands, and they improve automatically as you use them.

myplugins.title: My Plugins
myplugins.body: Manage installed plugins. A plugin is a bundle of skills — install one and the agent becomes an expert in that domain.

connectors.title: Connectors
connectors.body: Connect external services like Google Drive and Notion. Once connected, plugins use them automatically.

skills-market.title: Skill Market
skills-market.body: Find community-built skills and install them instantly. Add all kinds of workflows in one click.

plugins-market.title: Plugin Market
plugins-market.body: Browse plugins that bring domain expertise. Add specialists for areas like legal, data analysis, and workflow automation.

settings.title: Settings
settings.body: Reconfigure model connections and app preferences anytime. Even after onboarding, you can change or add AI models here.

screen-myskills-overview.title: Skill information
screen-myskills-overview.body: See the skill's purpose, usage count, and last-used date at a glance. Start here to get a quick read on what this skill does.

screen-myskills-overview-tab.title: Overview
screen-myskills-overview-tab.body: Review the skill's execution steps and the tools it uses. This shows how the skill carries out its work from start to finish.

screen-myskills-insights.title: Insights
screen-myskills-insights.body: Dive into real usage history, success and failure signals, friction points, routing issues, and AI analysis — the data that helps you improve each skill.

screen-myskills-manage.title: Skill management
screen-myskills-manage.body:
Three tools are available in this menu.
① Learning Impact — see how much a skill has improved your results
② Skill Cleanup — disable or archive rarely-used skills
③ AI Merge — detect overlapping skills and propose consolidations

screen-myskills-files.title: File browser
screen-myskills-files.body: Browse the actual file structure of a skill, including the raw Markdown source in SKILL.md. Useful for understanding and auditing exactly what the skill does.

screen-myskills-ai-edit.title: Edit with AI
screen-myskills-ai-edit.body: Request skill changes in plain language. Review the AI's proposed diff, then apply or reject it. Built-in skills provided by RICE cannot be edited with AI.

screen-myplugins-skills.title: Skills
screen-myplugins-skills.body: The executable skills this plugin provides. Each can be called with a / command in chat or used automatically via routing.

screen-myplugins-knowledge.title: Knowledge
screen-myplugins-knowledge.body: Documents, data, and guides that the plugin references. The agent draws on this knowledge to answer more accurately.

screen-myplugins-permissions.title: Permissions (Connectors)
screen-myplugins-permissions.body: The connectors this plugin needs to run. Check which external services are required and whether they are already connected.

screen-connectors-kinds.title: Remote vs. local
screen-connectors-kinds.body: Remote: built-in services like Gmail, plus any Custom Connector you add via OAuth. Local: MCP servers running on your machine, registered and called on demand.

screen-connectors-add.title: Adding connectors
screen-connectors-add.body: Browse the built-in catalog to add a supported service, or paste a Custom Connector URL to register any OAuth-enabled MCP server. Use the Local tab to register a local MCP server.

screen-connectors-tool-groups.title: Tool categories
screen-connectors-tool-groups.body: After connecting, MCP tools are grouped by nature: read-only tools (get, list, search…) and write/execute/delete tools. Grant permissions by group or fine-tune them per tool.

screen-connectors-permissions.title: Tool permissions
screen-connectors-permissions.body: Three levels for every tool: ① Always allow — runs without HITL ② Approval required — the agent asks before executing ③ Blocked — the tool is never injected into the agent's context.
